quick_english: Now this entire worship is taught through the glorious Kaula method, for the fit ones mounted on firm resolve of exactly that awakened kind. On this point it is said in the Yogasaṃcāra and the rest: bliss is Brahman — in the body, established threefold at lips and lowest end.
Those who abandon it, not abiding in Brahman, are cut off from bliss.
Sacrificers of the wheel who feed on blissless artificial food —
both fall into dreadful hell. Therefore one should keep to this stance.
So through this stance there is Kula-sacrifice, and it is sixfold: in the outer, in the Śakti, in one's own body, in the couple, in breath, and in consciousness.
Among these, each later one is higher; each earlier one serves to give a taste for it.

For one desiring powers, the second, fourth, and fifth are to be performed in every way; for one desiring release the sixth is chief — though even for him the second and the rest are to be done on occasional rites as far as possible, and to complete the rite.
Of these, the outer is the altar, full of bliss; the hero's cup, a red cloth, or else the liṅga and the rest mentioned before.

There, with no need for bathing and the rest of the duties — purity gained by resting in full bliss alone — first, having contemplated the oneness of breath, consciousness, and body, one should utter the mantra twenty-seven times over crown, face, heart, secret place, and body, in forward and reverse order, since consciousness is Paramaśiva's own form: the fullness of the universe-course in the Supreme Lord — in the lower, in the middle, and in the highest alike.

For thus: from Māyā, person, nature, intellect beginning down to earth, twenty-seven tattvas — kalā and the rest included therein — and likewise in the knowledge-power in the middle state, the qualities of the Brahman-pentad, beginning with instant-ness, born-ness, and become-arisen-ness, are just twenty-seven in form — so state the glorious Lakulīśa masters.

In the highest too the Lord is five-powered: per power, five forms — so twenty-five powers. Mutually undivided, they are one power, still undivided — so, by a pervasion twenty-seven-formed, one should bind the buddhi-and-breath-formed flame of consciousness-fire with a single utterance alone, so that only Paramaśiva stays bound and it runs to nothing beyond the tantra. Penetrated thus, one should make the present offering-substance, house, directions, and supports made of that; then fill the offering vessel by the tuft-binding pervasion alone and worship it; with its drops worship the altars too; by joining left ring-finger with thumb, worship and satisfy the mantra-wheel on the body-wheels with its essence. Then up to breath; then fashion the trident-formed seat ending in the three powers on the altar — up to Māyā in the lettered auṃ-syllable fashion the seat ending in the three powers — up to Māyā in the lettered auṃ-syllable; thereupon the power to be worshipped, deliberation-formed. Thus, by a single utterance alone, having made the placing of support and supported, one should see the universe right there, even in the consciousness that has become the supported — and that too made of consciousness. Thus the universe by consciousness, and by that, her mutual enclosure comes about: arisen from consciousness, it comes to rest right there — since the universe arises from the knowable, and consciousness rests right there. Just this much is the consciousness-principle, attained through the twofold enclosure.
So it is said: having enclosed emission —
Then, having offered incense, smoke, wine, flowers and the rest down to self-surrender, having muttered in one's own rest, having gathered it in, one should cast it into water.
Thus the outer sacrifice.

Now for the Śakti. There, goddesses and heroes of the Śakti-circle being mutually of both natures — from the awakening of Śiva and Śakti spanning play's beginning to emission's end, through mutual activity, by the Supreme Lord's ordainment, in pure form — preeminence lies there. By this, even the distinguished wheel's Śakti-ness is explained. There, worship is by the tuft-binding pervasion alone, on the seat ending in the three powers; in the triangle, in the middle, the emission-power — but in the pervasion lies the distinction.
So in one's own body: in that very wheel; then in the sub-wheels beginning with the crown-aperture.
Now for the couple. This is the mark of the Śakti: like that, non-difference. Then, disregarding age, birth and the rest, from non-attachment — for identity is born of the transgressive pair.
From being arisen together with cause and effect, threefold — directly, or else as arranged — the two, having worshipped each other, make bliss proximate by satisfying.
One should worship the wheel according to its fitness, and likewise the following sub-wheel — outside with flowers and the rest, inward with perfumes, foods, wines and the rest.
Thus the state surging with the play of that bliss-mass; the host of sub-wheels dissolves from identity with the wheel.
In the relish of own-being at the time of unfolding of each enjoyment, gradually the sub-wheel goddesses enter the middle consciousness-wheel.
Whose power is won by filling the host of rays embodied in sub-wheel goddesses — having the nature of that power, like that — becomes mutually facing.
The agitation born of the throbbing entry into the upper abode of that pair agitates the sub-wheels too — then made of that, not separate.
Thus this couple, whose talk of difference is dissolved — just when, then through gradation and excellence she indeed is the collision of consciousness and emission.
The steady supreme abode of that — the both-natured vast world — bliss is neither calm nor arisen: the womb-cause of calm and arisen, the supreme Kaula.
Desiring the undivided station, one should make her consciousness one's own; then the calm-and-arisen-natured pair arises at once for power and power-bearer.
From self-and-other interpenetration, when calm and other — of the two, from two-naturedness — power, like that arisen one, nourishes emission; its bearer does not.
In her is the excellent Kula; then by her, among men, the taught yoga-collisions — then, in the twofold emission, in this calm-arisen abode, those who contemplate —
In the eastward one, mounted in the undivided station as emission-being — the arisen too is received mutually from mouths, from the chief mouth outward into the mouth.
The goddess-wheel becomes satisfied, giving powers, knowledge, and release; in the practice of calm one attains the calm Śiva — which here is the deity-wheel.
The void devoid of bliss — from bliss's own abode the offering — and the humming-thrilled with the taste of relishing outer states filled with own essence.
The sub-wheel surging with inner fullness reaches the wheel; then that too surges as before. Thus this emission is threefold in implied sense.
In the emission-abode, through relish, mantra-power bears each fruit in each consciousness-womb — three ways indeed.
On the cover of eternal rising auspiciousness resting within the triangle, on the lotus — never parted the stalk, rooted in the true sixteen-petalled lotus.
In the fire at the course of rubbing the pair of lotuses strung on the central stalk — from the collision of moon-beauty and sun-ray-floods in the middle.
From union with the three-petalled ruddy power-ray, in the middle, sprout-emission — thus, by the seal of the wondrous gathering of moon and sun, in a flash.
Performing within the order beginning with emission, one gains steadiness in the fourth — this in the entry of the sky-going seal, mutually, of one's own power and power-bearer.
Who would be made of relish in drinking, enjoyment, play, laughter and the rest — with unmanifest sound, roar, burst, hearing, tone, and tone's end.
That mantra-power, with unbroken unstruck ultimate realities — in rests of going and coming, in the ear, in the eye, in contact with the double mark.
In the yoga of their closing, called body's end — and in the couple, in the wheel — which unmanifest, throat-reaching from the heart-place between the breasts to the lip's end.
Having heard that lying between the two wheels, when agitation ends, they rest there — and thus this supreme eightfold Nāda-Bhairava.
Since she is light and sound, that pervasion, mantra-bearing, is called highest — in every act the knower's would be release while living.
Knowing that, liberated in scripture, a vessel of alien-Kula wisdom — the womb — one should make void-and-nonvoid abode, fire and wind in the single staff.
Having made the trident of one taste — essence abiding in essence as it were — doubt abandoned, riteless: I am not, thus contemplating.
Seeing the goddesses dwelling in the body — joy, agitation and the rest in consciousness-mass — the host of goddesses dwelling in the ear-eye-mouth-nose wheels.
Always seeing the grasper, by Khecarī one succeeds certainly.
In a far distant chasm, in a flash hurling one's own body — dwelling without violence, having drawn in both hands, gazing — one should practice this sky-going seal.
Thus this is the couple-sacrifice.
In the stated-pervaded breath, made of the universe — by the taught consciousness-pervasion, strengthening through offering libation, food, perfume, incense and the rest — is breath-sacrifice.
But rest's establishment is consciousness-sacrifice, already taught before.

Thus, having performed any one of these sacrifices — if the disciple becomes one whose heart is painted with such doubtlessness — then for him, preceded by seeing that sacrifice, needing no prior sesame-ghee offering, one should perform initiation by a glance, in the order of contemplation by the aforesaid pervasion; but at the occasional rite's end for indirect initiation and the rest, the earlier alone is the rule.
Merely by sacrifice-primacy is this.
In the guru's body is the seventh Kula-sacrifice, most excellent of all — it too, performed once before together with the sacrifices, fulfills all. Śivam.
